stages.name: Indigenous peoples
stages.desc: Iberian, Celtic, Ligurian, Libyan and Berber peoples hold the land and its coasts

stages.name: Phoenician / Carthaginian sphere
stages.desc: Phoenician ports and sea lanes, led more and more by Carthage

stages.name: Greek colonies
stages.desc: Greek cities and trading posts set the pace on the coast

stages.name: Etruscan sphere
stages.desc: The Etruscan city-states rule the land and the Tyrrhenian Sea

stages.name: Contested
stages.desc: Rival powers share or fight over the coast; no one dominates

states.name: France
timeline: Phocaean Greeks found Massalia among the Ligurian Segobriges
Phocaeans found Alalia on the east coast of Corsica
The Phocaeans abandon Alalia after the battle; Corsica passes to the Etruscans while Massalia holds the coast

states.name: Morocco
timeline: Mauri (Berber) peoples hold the land; Phoenician Lixus and Mogador trade on the Atlantic coast

states.name: Spain
timeline: Tartessos and the Iberian peoples rule; Phoenician Gadir, Malaka and Sexi trade on the south coast
Phocaean Greeks found Emporion and trade with Tartessos, in waters the Phoenicians long had to themselves
After Alalia, Greek ships rarely pass south of the Balearics; the far south turns to Gadir and Carthage

states.name: Libya
timeline: Greek Cyrene, founded about 631 BC from Thera, leads the east; Libyan peoples hold the interior
The Spartan prince Dorieus founds a colony at the Cinyps river, in the west
Libyans and Carthaginians drive Dorieus out: Carthage's coast in the west, Greek Cyrene in the east

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage, founded from Tyre by tradition in 814 BC, is becoming the leading Phoenician city of the west
Mago founds the family that leads Carthage's armies for generations
Carthage signs its first treaty with Rome

states.name: Italy
timeline: Etruscan cities rule from the Arno to Campania; Greek colonies line the south, Phoenicians hold western Sicily and Sardinia's ports
Pentathlus's Greeks are beaten at Lilybaeum by the Elymians and Phoenicians of western Sicily
Caere stones the Phocaean prisoners taken off Alalia
Greek Cumae throws back an Etruscan army: the first check to Etruscan power in Campania
Rome expels its Etruscan kings and signs a treaty with Carthage; Etruria, Greeks and Carthage share Italy's seas

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Libyan (Berber) peoples hold the land; Phoenician sailors keep small anchorages on the coast

states.name: Malta
timeline: Phoenician settlers and the sanctuary of Astarte at Tas-Silġ

events.title: Massalia founded
events.text: Phocaean Greeks land at the Lacydon inlet; by legend their leader Protis marries Gyptis, daughter of the Segobriges' king.

events.title: First sea victory
events.text: Thucydides records that the Phocaeans, while founding Massalia, beat the Carthaginians at sea.

events.title: Carthage rising
events.text: On its peninsula in the Gulf of Tunis, Tyre's colony is becoming the leading Phoenician city of the west.

events.title: Gadir and Tartessos
events.text: Phoenician Gadir trades for the silver of Tartessos, the kingdom of the lower Guadalquivir.

events.title: Phoenician Sardinia
events.text: Tharros, Sulcis and Nora line Sardinia's coasts; the Nuragic peoples hold the interior.

events.title: Motya
events.text: On an islet off western Sicily, Motya is the Phoenicians' base facing the Greek cities to the east.

events.title: Caere and Pyrgi
events.text: Caere, with its port at Pyrgi, is among the richest of the Etruscan city-states.

events.title: Lixus
events.text: Phoenician Lixus trades with the Mauri peoples of the Atlantic coast.

events.title: Astarte at Tas-Silġ
events.text: Sailors honour Astarte at Malta's Phoenician sanctuary of Tas-Silġ.

events.title: Greeks at Gravisca
events.text: Greek merchants set up a sanctuary at Gravisca, the port of Etruscan Tarquinia.

events.title: Pentathlus fails
events.text: Greeks from Cnidus and Rhodes try to settle at Lilybaeum and are beaten by Elymians and Phoenicians.

events.title: Lipara settled
events.text: Pentathlus's survivors settle the Lipari islands and fight off Etruscan pirates.

events.title: Rachgoun
events.text: Phoenician traders on an islet off western Algeria exchange goods with Libyan peoples.

events.title: Emporion founded
events.text: Phocaeans found Emporion, "the market", on the coast of Catalonia.

events.title: Cyrene beats Egypt
events.text: The Greeks of Cyrene rout an Egyptian army sent by Pharaoh Apries.

events.title: Alalia founded
events.text: Following an oracle, Phocaeans found Alalia on the east coast of Corsica.

events.title: Silver for walls
events.text: Arganthonius, king of Tartessos, gives the Phocaeans silver to wall their city, says Herodotus.

events.title: Malchus in Sardinia
events.text: According to Justin, the Carthaginian general Malchus is defeated in Sardinia and turns on Carthage itself.

events.title: Mago's dynasty
events.text: Mago, says the historian Justin, reforms Carthage's army; his sons and grandsons lead it for generations.

events.title: Refugees reach Alalia
events.text: Fleeing the Persian conquest of Phocaea, Greek families sail to Alalia and raid its neighbours for five years.

events.title: Battle of Alalia
events.text: Sixty Phocaean ships meet sixty Carthaginian and sixty Etruscan ships; the Greeks win but lose forty ships.

events.title: Stoning at Caere
events.text: The Etruscans of Caere lead the Phocaean prisoners out and stone them to death.

events.title: Alalia abandoned
events.text: The Phocaeans take their women and children from Alalia and sail for Rhegion.

events.title: Elea founded
events.text: From Rhegion the Phocaeans found Hyele, later Elea, on the coast south of Poseidonia.

events.title: Games for the dead
events.text: On Delphi's orders, Caere honours the dead Phocaeans with sacrifices, athletic games and horse races.

events.title: Etruscan Corsica
events.text: Etruscans take over Alalia, and Corsica pays them tribute in resin, wax and honey.

events.title: Wine up the Rhône
events.text: Greek wine and pottery from Massalia travel up the Rhône to Celtic hillforts such as Mont Lassois.

events.title: Wars in Sardinia
events.text: Mago's sons Hasdrubal and Hamilcar fight to bring Sardinia under Carthage; Hasdrubal dies of his wounds there.

events.title: Cumae holds
events.text: The Greeks of Cumae, led by Aristodemus, rout a great Etruscan army.

events.title: Massalia's fleet
events.text: In these decades, ancient writers say, Massalia's ships fought Carthaginian fleets over fishing grounds and trade.

events.title: Dorieus in Libya
events.text: The Spartan prince Dorieus founds a Greek colony at the Cinyps river, deep in Carthage's Libyan coast.

events.title: Dorieus expelled
events.text: In its third year the Macae, Libyans and Carthaginians drive the colony out.

events.title: Sybaris destroyed
events.text: Croton destroys its rival Sybaris, the richest Greek city of the south.

events.title: Dorieus killed
events.text: Trying again in western Sicily, Dorieus is killed by the Phoenicians and the Elymians of Segesta.

events.title: Temple at Pyrgi
events.text: Caere's port raises a temple where gold tablets in Etruscan and Phoenician honour Uni-Astarte.

events.title: Kings expelled
events.text: By Roman tradition, Rome drives out its last Etruscan king, Tarquin the Proud, and becomes a republic.

events.title: Treaty with Rome
events.text: Rome and Carthage swear a treaty, engraved on bronze and preserved by Polybius, that marks off their spheres.

events.title: Fair Promontory
events.text: Roman ships may not sail beyond the Fair Promontory near Carthage unless driven by storm or enemies.

events.title: Latin towns protected
events.text: Carthage promises not to harm Ardea, Antium, Circeii, Tarracina or other Latin towns subject to Rome.

chartNote: Share of the area of eight present-day countries, by the power that dominated their coasts. Today's borders stand in for a world of city-states and tribal lands; the vast Saharan interiors of Algeria and Libya swing the shares, and most dates before 500 BC are approximate. A simplification: each country held several peoples at once.
